parts.title: From Office to Orchard: One Woman's Journey into Farming
parts.directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.
passage: Linh spent eight years working as an accountant in a large company in the city. Her job paid well, but the long hours, heavy traffic, and constant deadlines left her **exhausted** at the end of every day. She often looked out of the office window at the grey buildings and wondered whether this was really the life she wanted. One weekend, while visiting her uncle's village, she walked through his small orchard of mango and orange trees and felt calmer than she had for months.

After that visit, Linh could not stop thinking about the orchard and the quiet life it offered. Her friends said that farming was hard and that she knew nothing about plants, but she decided to find out the truth. She saved money for two years, took a short course on fruit growing, and spent her holidays helping her uncle prepare the soil, water the young trees, and pick the fruit. In the end, she resigned from her job and bought a small piece of land near his village, which her family thought was a risky choice.

The first year was much harder than Linh had imagined. She woke at five every morning, and her hands became rough from digging, planting, and carrying water. Heavy rain damaged some of the young trees, and insects ate many of the leaves. Fruit trees take several years to produce a good harvest, so Linh's income grew **gradually**, and for a long time she earned much less than she had in the city. During this time she lived simply, ate vegetables from her own garden, and learned from neighbours who had farmed all their lives.

Over time, her hard work and patience began to pay off in several ways. Linh learned to use natural fertiliser, protect the trees from insects without too many chemicals, and sell her fruit directly to customers through social media. She also invited families to visit the orchard at weekends and pick fruit for themselves, which brought extra money and helped city children see where food comes from. Looking back, Linh says that she taught **herself** most of what she knows, although the advice of her uncle and neighbours was always valuable.

Today, Linh's orchard produces mangoes, oranges, and a small amount of vegetables, and she employs two part-time workers from the village. She is not rich, but she says that she is healthier and happier than in the office. Her mango trees, which were tiny when she planted them, are now taller than she is. Her story shows that a big change in life is possible when a person is patient, willing to learn, and ready to accept some risk. Many people dream of leaving a stressful job, and Linh hopes that her experience will encourage others to follow a dream that matters to them.

parts.title: Staying Well in Lockdown: Health-Promoting Activities During the COVID-19 Pandemic
parts.directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.
passage: When governments introduced lockdowns in 2020 to slow the spread of COVID-19, millions of people suddenly found their daily routines disrupted. Offices, schools, gyms, and cafés closed, and many people spent most of their time at home. Health experts soon pointed out that staying safe from the virus was only one part of staying well, since physical and mental health could suffer when people became inactive and isolated.

Physical activity was the first priority. The World Health Organization recommends that adults do at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity physical activity each week and avoid long periods of **sedentary** behaviour. During lockdowns, many people followed online exercise classes, walked or cycled near their homes where this was allowed, and used simple equipment such as stairs, chairs, and bottles of water. Studies suggest that regular exercise is linked to lower levels of depression and anxiety, and to better sleep.

Diet and sleep also mattered. With restaurants closed and shopping trips limited, many households cooked at home more often, which gave some people the chance to eat more fresh food and others a reason to rely on snacks. Nutrition experts generally advise a balanced diet with plenty of vegetables, fruit, and water. Keeping regular sleeping hours was equally important, because irregular schedules, long hours of screen time, and late-night news can all disturb rest. A simple daily routine, with fixed times for meals, work, exercise, and rest, helps people to **sustain** healthy habits when everything else feels uncertain.

Mental health required deliberate attention. Isolation left many people lonely, so video calls, messaging groups, and distanced meetings with friends became lifelines. Some people also tried mindfulness, meditation, or breathing exercises, which research suggests may reduce stress in some individuals, although the evidence varies. Others limited their exposure to distressing news, checking trusted sources once or twice a day instead of following every update, because constant alerts can increase anxiety.

Hobbies and learning gave days a sense of purpose. Online platforms offered free or low-cost courses, and libraries and museums made books, tours, and exhibitions available to anyone with an internet connection. Many people baked bread, gardened on balconies, painted, played instruments, or studied languages online, and some discovered skills that **they** had never had time to develop before. Learning something new also gave people a goal to look forward to each week.

Not everyone could follow this advice, however. People who lived in crowded housing, lost their jobs, or cared for children without help often had little space, time, or money for exercise and hobbies. Health authorities therefore stressed that small, realistic steps were better than perfect plans. Anyone who felt overwhelmed was encouraged to seek professional support.

In the end, staying well in lockdown depended on a mixture of movement, rest, connection, and purpose. Although the pandemic was a difficult period, it showed that ordinary daily choices can protect both body and mind, and many of the habits people formed have remained useful long after restrictions ended. The lesson for the future is that health is not only the absence of illness but also the result of the routines and relationships that support us every day.

parts.title: Learning at Home: The Rise of Parent-Led Education
parts.directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.
passage: Education has traditionally been associated with schools, teachers, and timetables, yet a growing number of families have chosen a more **unconventional** path by teaching their children at home. Home education is not a new idea, but the recent growth in numbers has raised questions about learning, parental responsibility, and the role of the state. This passage examines how it developed, why families choose it, and what the evidence shows.

Until roughly the nineteenth century, most children were educated at home or through apprenticeship, and formal schooling for the majority is a relatively recent development. Compulsory attendance laws passed in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries moved education into classrooms, although some isolated communities continued to teach at home. Modern homeschooling is usually traced to the 1960s and 1970s, when reformers criticised industrialised schooling. The American educator John Holt, who coined the term unschooling, argued that children learn best when their own curiosity directs them.

In the United States, the number of homeschooled children grew from roughly 10,000 families in 1979 to nearly 500,000 by the late 1980s, according to estimates cited in the literature. Before the COVID-19 pandemic, about three per cent of students were taught at home, and survey data suggest that the share had roughly doubled by the 2023–24 school year. Closed schools and health fears probably explained part of the increase, although exact figures are uncertain.

Families choose home education for a variety of reasons. **[1]** Some are dissatisfied with the academic quality of local schools, or worry about bullying and safety. **[2]** Others want greater control over the curriculum, including the moral or religious instruction their children receive. **[3]** Such circumstances rarely suit a rigid timetable, so flexibility often matters more to these parents than any particular teaching method. **[4]** Religion was once the most commonly cited motive in the United States, and one survey reportedly found that the proportion fell from nearly two-thirds of parents in 2012 to about one-third in 2023.

Legal treatment varies enormously. In the United States, home education is legal in every state, but the rules range from minimal oversight to registration and testing. Germany enforces compulsory attendance at school strictly, whereas France has narrowed **its** rules since 2022 so that home education is allowed only in specific circumstances. In Ontario, children may be exempt from school if they receive satisfactory instruction at home. South Africa requires registration and regular assessment.

Evidence about outcomes is limited and contested. Many studies rely on small, convenient samples, and several were supported by advocacy groups, so few are truly **rigorous** by the standards of educational research. A 2022 review reportedly found no systematic evidence of poor outcomes, but could not draw firm conclusions. Some studies suggest that homeschooled students do slightly better in reading and writing and slightly worse in mathematics, while findings on university attendance are mixed.

parts.title: Silicon and Ambition: Dell, Nvidia, and the Infrastructure of Artificial Intelligence
parts.directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.
passage: Public discussion of artificial intelligence often focuses on software, such as chatbots and image generators, but these tools rest on a vast physical foundation of chips, servers, data centres, and electricity. Companies that build this hardware **underpin** the industry, although their names are less familiar. Two of the most prominent are Nvidia, which designs the accelerators that train and run AI models, and Dell Technologies, which assembles many of the servers that host the accelerators.

Nvidia was founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem, initially to build graphics chips for video games. Its GeForce 256, released in 1999, was the first product the company marketed as a graphics processing unit. The decisive step came in the 2000s, when Nvidia reportedly invested more than a billion dollars in CUDA, a software platform that lets programmers use graphics chips for general parallel computing.

As AI models grew larger, demand for Nvidia's accelerators surged dramatically across the industry. By 2025 the company reportedly controlled more than 80 per cent of the market for chips used to train and deploy AI models, and its sales of data-centre products dwarfed its original gaming business. Its market value rose from about one trillion dollars in 2023 to reportedly more than four trillion dollars by July 2025, a rise that made it one of the most valuable companies.

Dell Technologies has a very different history. Michael Dell founded the company as a personal-computer maker, and it grew by selling directly to customers. After going private in 2013, Dell acquired the storage company EMC in a deal reportedly valued at roughly 67 billion dollars, which created the present company in 2016. Dell returned to the stock market in December 2018, and its Infrastructure Solutions Group, covering servers, storage, and networking, accounted for about 38 per cent of revenue in fiscal 2024.

Dell's role in this ecosystem is to turn components into working systems. [1] It builds servers that combine Nvidia's accelerators with its own networking, storage, and cooling technology, and sells the integrated systems to businesses and governments that lack the expertise to assemble such hardware. **[2]** Dell, for its part, wins access to the most sought-after accelerators, although this closeness also makes it dependent on a single supplier. **[3]** The scale of that partnership became clear in 2025, when Dell reported confirmed orders for AI-optimised servers worth about 14 billion dollars. **[4]** Executives nevertheless described demand as lumpy and nonlinear, because large orders depend on customers' data-centre construction, power supplies, and cooling.

Building AI infrastructure is harder than assembling ordinary servers. Dell has reportedly said that one rack of Nvidia's GB200 NVL72 design contains roughly 1.2 million parts, and sourcing and assembling them depends on suppliers, construction, power, and liquid cooling. Geopolitics adds a further complication, since United States rules introduced in October 2022 restricted exports of the most advanced data-centre chips to China, and Nvidia responded with modified products that complied. Together, these pressures make the business more volatile than the enthusiasm around AI might suggest.

Whether this boom lasts is uncertain. The answer will shape not only corporate profits but also the pace of technological change. Optimists argue that AI will enter every industry, so demand for computing power will keep growing, while sceptics point to heavy spending, concentrated suppliers, and the risk that expectations have outrun profits. What is clear is that the visible face of AI depends on a hidden industrial base, and that the companies controlling it hold unusual influence over how quickly the technology spreads.

tasks.guide_md:
**1. Phân tích đề bài và xác định dạng bài:**
- Đây là dạng bài **Advantages and Disadvantages Essay**, yêu cầu phân tích cả mặt tích cực và tiêu cực của online shopping.
- Từ khóa quan trọng cần xác định là advantages, disadvantages và online shopping. Không nên chỉ tập trung vào lợi ích hoặc chỉ nêu hạn chế.
- Bài viết cần tối thiểu **250 từ** và được đánh giá dựa trên khả năng trả lời đúng yêu cầu, tổ chức ý tưởng, từ vựng và ngữ pháp.

**2. Cách xây dựng bố cục (Organization):**
- **Introduction:** Giới thiệu xu hướng mua sắm trực tuyến và nêu rằng nó có cả ưu điểm lẫn nhược điểm. Ví dụ: Online shopping has changed the way people purchase goods in modern society.
- **Body 1:** Trình bày các advantages. Cấu trúc đoạn nên gồm câu chủ đề, giải thích, ví dụ và câu kết nối. Ví dụ: One major advantage of online shopping is its convenience.
- **Body 2:** Trình bày các disadvantages. Có thể đề cập đến vấn đề chất lượng sản phẩm, bảo mật thông tin hoặc ảnh hưởng đến cửa hàng truyền thống.
- **Body 3:** Có thể bổ sung đoạn đánh giá tổng quát nếu cần, nhưng không bắt buộc.
- **Conclusion:** Tóm tắt hai mặt của vấn đề. Ví dụ: In conclusion, online shopping offers great convenience, but consumers should be aware of its potential drawbacks.

**3. Chiến lược đạt điểm cao (Vocabulary & Grammar):**
- Sử dụng thì hiện tại đơn để mô tả xu hướng và sự thật chung về mua sắm trực tuyến.
- Mỗi ý chính cần được mở rộng bằng giải thích và ví dụ cụ thể để tránh viết chung chung.
- Cần có câu luận điểm rõ ràng ở phần mở bài và sử dụng từ nối để tạo sự liên kết giữa các đoạn.
Từ vựng quan trọng:
- **Online shopping:** Mua sắm trực tuyến
- **E-commerce platform:** Nền tảng thương mại điện tử
- **Convenience:** Sự tiện lợi
- **Consumer behavior:** Hành vi người tiêu dùng
- **Product quality:** Chất lượng sản phẩm
- **Privacy protection:** Bảo vệ quyền riêng tư
Từ nối (Linking words):
- **Furthermore:** Hơn nữa (thêm ý)
- **In addition:** Ngoài ra (thêm ý)
- **However:** Tuy nhiên (đối lập)
- **On the other hand:** Mặt khác (so sánh)
- **As a result:** Vì vậy (kết quả)
- **For example:** Ví dụ (minh họa)
Diễn đạt lại ý (Paraphrasing):
- **Online shopping:** Có thể thay bằng e-commerce hoặc digital shopping để tránh lặp từ.
- **Advantages:** Có thể dùng benefits, positive aspects hoặc strengths.
- **Disadvantages:** Có thể dùng drawbacks, negative impacts hoặc limitations.
Cách diễn đạt ý kiến / so sánh / giải pháp:
- **One of the main benefits is that:** Dùng để giới thiệu một lợi ích chính.
- **A major drawback is that:** Dùng để trình bày một hạn chế quan trọng.
- **Despite these disadvantages, I believe that:** Dùng để đưa ra đánh giá cân bằng.

**4. Các lỗi thường gặp:**
- Chỉ viết về ưu điểm mà không phân tích nhược điểm, dẫn đến không đáp ứng dạng bài.
- Liệt kê quá nhiều ý nhưng không giải thích hoặc đưa ví dụ.
- Sử dụng từ vựng không phù hợp hoặc lặp lại online shopping quá nhiều lần.

**5. Cách kiểm tra bài trong 3–5 phút cuối:**
- Kiểm tra đã có đủ phần mở bài, hai đoạn thân bài và kết luận chưa.
- Đảm bảo cả advantages và disadvantages đều được đề cập.
- Rà soát lỗi ngữ pháp, chính tả, số từ và sự liên kết giữa các đoạn.

**6. Tư duy làm bài:**
- Hãy tập trung vào việc phát triển ý tưởng rõ ràng thay vì cố sử dụng quá nhiều từ khó.
- Một bài luận tốt cần thể hiện khả năng phân tích cân bằng giữa các mặt của vấn đề.
- Luôn lập dàn ý ngắn trước khi viết để đảm bảo bài có cấu trúc logic và đầy đủ nội dung.

parts.prompt:
SPEAKING — PART 1

Questions:

Let’s talk about a good friend

1
Do you have a close friend? Please tell me about him or her.
2
What qualities do you think make a good friend?
3
How has your good friend influenced your life?

Now, let’s talk about public events

4
Do you often attend public events in your area?
5
What kinds of public events do you enjoy the most?
6
Do you think public events are important for local communities? Why?
parts.guide_md:
**1. Phân tích đề bài:**
- Phần này gồm 6 câu hỏi trong khoảng 3 phút, kiểm tra khả năng giao tiếp tự nhiên và phản xạ ngôn ngữ của bạn.
- **Topic A (Good Friend):** Các câu hỏi 1–3 tập trung vào bạn bè thân thiết, phẩm chất của một người bạn tốt và ảnh hưởng của tình bạn đối với cuộc sống.
- **Topic B (Public Events):** Các câu hỏi 4–6 tập trung vào các sự kiện công cộng, hoạt động cộng đồng và quan điểm của bạn về vai trò của chúng.
- Giám khảo đánh giá độ trôi chảy, từ vựng, ngữ pháp và phát âm.
- Nên dành khoảng 25–35 giây cho mỗi câu hỏi và phân bổ thời gian cân bằng giữa hai chủ đề.

**2. Cách xây dựng bố cục khi nói (Organization):**
- Sử dụng cấu trúc ARE: Answer – Reason – Example để mở rộng câu trả lời.
- **Ví dụ Topic A:** I have a close friend named Minh because he is always supportive. For example, he helped me prepare for an important exam last year.
- **Ví dụ Topic B:** I enjoy attending music festivals because they are entertaining and help me meet new people.
- Luôn tự hỏi Why? hoặc How? để phát triển ý tưởng.
- Khi chuyển chủ đề có thể dùng câu: Speaking of social activities, I would also like to talk about public events.

**3. Chiến lược đạt điểm cao (Fluency, Vocabulary & Grammar):**
- Duy trì tốc độ nói ổn định và sử dụng các cụm đệm tự nhiên khi cần thêm thời gian suy nghĩ.
- Chủ đề bạn bè thường dùng hiện tại đơn và quá khứ đơn khi kể trải nghiệm.
- Chủ đề sự kiện công cộng có thể dùng hiện tại đơn và tương lai đơn khi nói về kế hoạch.
- Nếu quên từ vựng, hãy diễn đạt bằng từ đơn giản hơn thay vì dừng lại.
- Từ vựng Topic A: close friend (bạn thân), supportive (hay giúp đỡ), trustworthy (đáng tin cậy), get along well (hòa hợp).
- Từ vựng Topic B: community event (sự kiện cộng đồng), cultural festival (lễ hội văn hóa), public gathering (buổi tụ họp công cộng), social interaction (tương tác xã hội).
Cụm từ quan trọng nên dùng:
- A shoulder to lean on – chỗ dựa tinh thần.
- Have a lot in common – có nhiều điểm chung.
- Stand by someone – luôn ở bên ai đó.
- Bring people together – gắn kết mọi người.
- Promote community spirit – thúc đẩy tinh thần cộng đồng.
- Provide entertainment opportunities – mang lại cơ hội giải trí.
Từ nối khi nói (Linking Words):
- Firstly – đầu tiên.
- Besides that – bên cạnh đó.
- For example – ví dụ.
- As a result – kết quả là.
- In addition – thêm vào đó.
Cách thể hiện quan điểm tự nhiên:
- In my opinion, a good friend should be honest. – Theo tôi, một người bạn tốt nên trung thực.
- I personally believe that friendship is very important. – Cá nhân tôi tin rằng tình bạn rất quan trọng.
- From my experience, supportive friends make life easier. – Theo kinh nghiệm của tôi, những người bạn hỗ trợ nhau giúp cuộc sống dễ dàng hơn.
- I think public events are beneficial because they connect people. – Tôi nghĩ các sự kiện công cộng có ích vì chúng kết nối mọi người.
- As far as I am concerned, local festivals should be encouraged. – Theo quan điểm của tôi, các lễ hội địa phương nên được khuyến khích.
- I would say community activities improve social relationships. – Tôi cho rằng hoạt động cộng đồng cải thiện các mối quan hệ xã hội.

**4. Các lỗi thường gặp:**
- Trả lời Yes hoặc No rồi dừng lại mà không giải thích.
- Chỉ mô tả bạn bè bằng các từ đơn giản như nice hoặc good.
- Nói quá chung chung về sự kiện công cộng mà không đưa ví dụ cụ thể.
- Dùng sai thì khi kể lại trải nghiệm trong quá khứ.

**5. Chiến lược xử lý khi bí ý hoặc quên từ:**
- Dùng câu đệm: That is an interesting question, let me think for a second.
- Mô tả từ bằng ý nghĩa nếu quên từ chính xác.
- Với Topic A, hãy kể một kỷ niệm với bạn thân để kéo dài câu trả lời.
- Với Topic B, hãy nói về một sự kiện bạn từng tham gia hoặc muốn tham gia.

**6. Tư duy làm bài nói:**
- Hãy xem đây là một cuộc trò chuyện tự nhiên với giám khảo.
- Khi chuyển từ Topic A sang Topic B, hãy thay đổi trọng tâm sang hoạt động cộng đồng.
- Sự tự nhiên và mạch lạc quan trọng hơn việc cố dùng từ vựng quá khó.

- Ba phương án gồm chi phí, diện tích và vị trí.

- Thời gian khoảng 4 phút, nên dành 1 phút chuẩn bị và 3 phút trình bày.

**2. Cách xây dựng bố cục khi nói (Organization):**
- Sử dụng cấu trúc State opinion – Give reason – Compare – Conclude.
- Option 1: Giá thấp giúp giảm áp lực tài chính nhưng có thể thiếu tiện ích.
- Option 2: Nhà rộng tạo không gian thoải mái nhưng thường đắt hơn.
- Option 3: Vị trí tốt thuận tiện đi lại và tăng giá trị lâu dài.

- Dùng từ nối tương phản khi chuyển giữa ưu điểm và nhược điểm.

**3. Chiến lược đạt điểm cao (Fluency, Vocabulary & Grammar):**
- Luôn liên kết các lựa chọn với nhau thay vì nói riêng lẻ.
- Dùng hiện tại đơn để đánh giá các lựa chọn và điều kiện để giả định kết quả.
- Nếu quên từ chuyên ngành bất động sản, hãy diễn đạt bằng ngôn ngữ đơn giản.
Cụm từ quan trọng nên dùng:
- Affordable housing – nhà ở có giá phải chăng.
- Financial burden – gánh nặng tài chính.
- Living space – không gian sinh hoạt.
- Convenient transportation – giao thông thuận tiện.
- Long-term investment – khoản đầu tư dài hạn.
- Property value – giá trị bất động sản.
Từ nối khi nói (Linking Words):
- On the one hand – một mặt.
- On the other hand – mặt khác.
- However – tuy nhiên.
- In contrast – trái lại.
- Therefore – vì vậy.
Cách thể hiện quan điểm tự nhiên:
- I would choose a good location because it offers long-term benefits. – Tôi sẽ chọn vị trí tốt vì mang lại lợi ích lâu dài.
